earlier_scan.source_named: Cohen, Kevin Bretonnel. 2000. Aspects of the Grammar of Kuku. Munich: Lincom Europa, 162 pp. (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description grammar; Kuku is tonal per secondary sources); no online copy found.

tone_statements.citation: Aburi, Laboka Basil Modi, et al. (Kuku Community Trust). 2019. ISO 639-3 Registration Authority Change Request Number 2019-045: Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code (split Kuku from Bari [bfa]; form dated 2019-5-1, 38 pp.), with the companion form 'Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Kuku [ukv]' (dated 2019-09-01, 12 pp.); outcome 'Partially Adopted', [ukv] Kuku created effective 2020-01-23 (RA comments, 2 pp.). Dallas: SIL International / ISO 639-3 RA.
tone_statements.quote: Some cultural and socio-linguistic manner and mannerism of speech of some Bari-speaking communities is abusive and is one of the components which make Kuku different from Bari. As a tonal language with extensive use of glottal stops sound inventory at the advanced tongue root, the Kuku use verbal morphology with extensive supplication.
tone_statements.locator: CR 2019-045 form, p. 8, rationale item (c) (quoted); also p. 18, end of the section 'The developed Kuku orthography and system of writing': 'The differences between Kuku and Bari include the phoneme inventory and tonal phonology as demonstrated above'; companion [ukv] form p. 10: 'Kuku speech and its tonality emanate from the advance tongue root (ATR) and the vocal cords.'
tone_statements.summary: Kuku is asserted to be a tonal language whose tonal phonology differs from Bari's; no inventory or analysis given (community document).

sources.note: Secondary: 'Kuku is a tone language'; differences from Bari include 'tonal phonology' (cites Cohen 2000, no page). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page and JSON for kuku1285 (Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Cohen 2000 grammar; Vanden Plas 1910 a wordlist or less; also Vossen 1982, Eberhard et al. 2025).
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Confirms Cohen 2000 is the sole grammar-level description; no phonology-typed reference exists for Kuku.

sources.citation: Vossen, Rainer. 1982. The Eastern Nilotes: Linguistic and Historical Reconstructions (Kölner Beiträge zur Afrikanistik 9). Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. Rosetta Project excerpts pp. 158-162 (sec. 7.1, informants) and pp. 173-174 (sec. 7.2.1.1 Bari phonology).
sources.note: Sec. 7.1.3 Kuku (p. 160): 'All data on Ku are my own due to lack of published sources' (informant Henry Koda, Kajo Kaji). Sec. 7.2.1.1.3 Tone (p. 174, Bari proper): lexical and grammatical tone, H/L/M/HL(/LR) after Yokwe 1977/78; nothing on stress. The BARI-dialects section (7.2.1.2), where Kuku data would sit, is cut off by the excerpt; full book not open.

sources.citation: Spagnolo, Fr. Lorenzo M. 1933. Bari Grammar. Verona: Missioni Africane. Rosetta Project excerpt (para. 14 sound chart only).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KG 9661)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KG 9661
sources.note: Excerpt is the alphabet/sound chart only; nothing on accent or stress visible. Full book not open. Bari proper, not Kuku.

sources.citation: Vanden Plas, Joseph (with Cyrille van Overbergh). 1910. Les Kuku (possessions anglo-égyptiennes) (Collection de monographies ethnographiques). Bruxelles: A. Dewit. 225 pp. (GlottologGlottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist for kuku1285).
sources.note: Ethnographic monograph; language content is only 'Vocabulaire du dialecte parlé par les Kuku' (numerals, body parts, animals) with no accent marks and no remarks on pronunciation, accent or tone. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Owen, R. C. R. (ed.). 1908. Bari Grammar and Vocabulary. London: J. & E. Bumpus. (Bari of Mongalla Province / Juba, bari1284; full public-domain text plus Rosetta phonology excerpt.)
sources.note: NOT Kuku (Kuku not mentioned). Part I paras. 15-17 'Quantities and Accents': (a) Word-Accents: many words have 'the same accent' on every vowel, in others 'one syllable is especially prominent, namely, in all imperatives'; (b) Sentence-Accent (enclitics). Pre-modern accent notation conflating pitch and prominence; no word-stress rule.

sources.citation: Mitterrutzner, J. C. 1867. Die Sprache der Bari in Central-Afrika: Grammatik, Text und Wörterbuch. Brixen: Weger. (Bari proper, bari1284.)
sources.note: NOT Kuku. §16 and §40 'Die Betonung': many polysyllables with 'gleicher Tonhöhe aller Sylben' (equal pitch on all syllables), others with one accented syllable; the accent of the durative stays on the same syllable in aorist/future. Tone described as 'accent'; no stress rule.

sources.citation: Aburi, Laboka Basil Modi, et al. (Kuku Community Trust). 2019. ISO 639-3 Registration Authority Change Request Number 2019-045: Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code (split Kuku from Bari [bfa]; form dated 2019-5-1, 38 pp.), with the companion form 'Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Kuku [ukv]' (dated 2019-09-01, 12 pp.); outcome 'Partially Adopted', [ukv] Kuku created effective 2020-01-23 (RA comments, 2 pp.). Dallas: SIL International / ISO 639-3 RA.
sources.quote: Some cultural and socio-linguistic manner and mannerism of speech of some Bari-speaking communities is abusive and is one of the components which make Kuku different from Bari. As a tonal language with extensive use of glottal stops sound inventory at the advanced tongue root, the Kuku use verbal morphology with extensive supplication.
sources.locator: CR 2019-045 form, p. 8, rationale item (c) (quoted); also p. 18, end of the section 'The developed Kuku orthography and system of writing': 'The differences between Kuku and Bari include the phoneme inventory and tonal phonology as demonstrated above'; companion [ukv] form p. 10: 'Kuku speech and its tonality emanate from the advance tongue root (ATR) and the vocal cords.'
sources.note: The requesters assert that Kuku is 'a tonal language' (p. 8) and that Kuku differs from Bari in 'the phoneme inventory and tonal phonology' (p. 18, echoing Cohen 2000 / Wikipedia wording); the companion form adds the folk-phonetic remark that 'Kuku speech and its tonality emanate from the advance tongue root (ATR) and the vocal cords' (p. 10) and that Bari speakers 'generally have high pitch tone and speak very fast' (p. 8). No tone inventory, no tone-bearing unit, no tone marking in the proposed orthography (the apostrophe marks glottal stops, not tone), no examples of tonal contrast. A lay,…

sources.citation: Yokwe, Eluzai Moga. 1987. The Tonal Grammar of Bari. PhD dissertation, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Fullest tonal analysis of Bari proper (Kuku's closest relative, often treated as a Bari dialect); would supply the prosodic frame (tone vs. stress) for the Bari cluster. Bari, not Kuku.
